key_insight: Single-person ERP detectability varied widely by task, with lower detection rates in minimally conscious patients than in healthy controls.
clinical_relevance: ERP testing may reveal residual cognitive processing, but a negative result cannot reliably establish its absence.
method: Tested six auditory ERP paradigms in 48 healthy controls and 26 minimally conscious patients.
Compared blinded visual scoring, ROI ANOVA, cluster-based permutation tests, and support vector machine decoding.
Assessed associations with recovery in 22 surviving patients at follow-up.
evidence_signal: Visual scoring detected passive and active oddball P300 in all 48 controls, versus 35% and 31% of patients, respectively; visual scoring and machine learning generally detected more effects than statistical tests.
watch_item: Detection depended on task and analysis method, and the truncated abstract does not provide a complete prognostic conclusion.
paper_title: Benchmarking single-subject detectability of cognitive event-related potentials in healthy controls and minimally conscious state patients
